content.text: As a general rule, it would be best if Fedora did not need superuser permissions to run
: Certainly this is an important bug to fix. Is it needed by one of the migration pilot partners? I am wondering if this is actually a Beta-blocker.
I'm going to record a video on fcrepo-aws-deployer on Monday and I need this to be fixed.  I've testing my final fix now.
Plus how much would it suck if a user were trying to run their fedora on AWS RDS  using the recommended database (postgresql) only to have it just fail to start.

The problem is that we are trying to disable triggers in order to truncate the search tables when doing so requires super user control of the database.  In RDS, since AWS partially manages the instance, some super user permissions are not available to the root user.
Caused by: org.fcrepo.kernel.api.exception.RepositoryRuntimeException: Failed to truncate search index tables

Caused by: java.sql.BatchUpdateException: Batch entry 0 ALTER TABLE search_resource_rdf_type DISABLE TRIGGER ALL was aborted: ERROR: permission denied: "RI_ConstraintTrigger_c_16508" is a system trigger  Call getNextException to see other errors in the batch.
Caused by: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: ERROR: permission denied: "RI_ConstraintTrigger_c_16508" is a system trigger
